McLaren.summary: McLaren’s latest upgrade adds a small winglet to the rear‑brake duct, reshaping the airflow around the rear corner of the car. This tweak keeps the brakes cooler and smooths the air that feeds the rear diffuser, giving the car a little extra rear‑end stability and grip. In practice, it should translate into better cornering speed and more consistent performance over the whole race weekend.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls has added a few extra front‑wing settings so the team can fine‑tune the car’s balance for this circuit, giving drivers more grip in the corners without losing straight‑line speed. They’ve also introduced a new two‑element beam wing with a more aggressive shape, which trims drag and helps the car stay stable on the long straights. Together, these tweaks should let the RB car be both more nimble through the twisty sections and quicker on the back‑markers, boosting its overall competitiveness this weekend.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams is bringing a brand‑new rear beam wing to the weekend, specially tuned for this circuit’s drag requirements. By tweaking the wing’s angle, the car will either slice through the straights faster or gain a little extra stability in the corners, depending on what the track demands. In short, the update should give the team a better balance between top‑speed and grip, helping them extract more performance from the car this weekend.

Sauber / Audi.summary: Sauber’s Audi‑powered car gets a freshly reshaped engine cover – the “Coke” flow‑conditioning piece has been tweaked to smooth the air that passes over the rear of the car. By cleaning up that airflow the team hopes to gain a bit more down‑force and a cleaner rear‑end, which should translate into better tyre grip and higher cornering speeds for this weekend’s race. In short, a modest aero tweak that could give Sauber the extra bite they need on the track.
